items.statement: A counter notice requires a good-faith belief that removal resulted from mistake or misidentification.
The counter notice is sworn under penalty of perjury.
Intentionally false sworn information can cause criminal and civil consequences.
The complainant may sue to keep the material disabled if they dispute the counter notice.
A DMCA notice is for a specific copyrightable work, not a trademark or sensitive-data complaint.
The complainant should investigate the allegation before filing.
A code repository may contain only a file or subroutine that infringes rather than an entire repository.
Open-source licenses can authorize use even when code bears a copyright notice.
A particular code use may qualify as fair use and must be considered separately.
Internal server names, IP addresses, or URLs alone do not qualify without a shown security threat.
A mere mention of a company name or brand does not qualify without an articulated security threat.
An objectionable full file or repository does not qualify if it poses no specific security risk.
The report must identify the reported account username.
The report must provide the trademark registration number.
The report must identify the trademark registration office.
The report must describe the confusion caused by the reported use.
The report must state the requested action.
The report must include a good-faith statement addressing authorization and fair uses.
A counter notice must identify the disabled content and its prior URL.
It must provide the submitter's email, name, phone, and physical address.
It must include a sworn good-faith belief that removal was a mistake or misidentification.
It must consent to the specified federal court's jurisdiction and accept service of process.
It must include a physical or electronic signature.
The complaint must identify the copyrighted work claimed to be infringed.
It must identify allegedly infringing material specifically enough for GitHub to locate it, including a URL at minimum.
It must explain what the affected user needs to do to remedy the infringement.
It must give the complainant's contact information.
It must include a good-faith statement considering authorization and fair use.
Contacting the user first is encouraged but is not required.
The process is an exceptional service for high-risk content and cannot handle unrelated removal requests at the same time.
Multiple or additional requests can delay review.
The online DMCA form is the fastest way to get a response.
Email submissions should include a plain-text version in the email body even if attached.
Physical mail takes substantially longer to receive and process.
The 10–14 day waiting period begins when GitHub receives the counter notice.
The claim concerns a technological measure that effectively controls access to a copyright-protected work.
The claim must describe the technical measure in question.
The claim must describe how the measure effectively controls access to copyrighted material.
The claim must describe how the accused project is designed to circumvent that measure.
GitHub does not automatically disable forks when it disables a parent repository.
GitHub does not independently investigate forks; the copyright owner must do so.
A valid claim identifying all then-existing forks may be processed against the network's forks.
The private-information process also does not automatically disable forks with the parent.
A private-information requester must investigate and identify forks containing the reported information.
GitHub prohibits using the platform to organize, promote, threaten, or incite violence.
GitHub prohibits content that depicts or glorifies physical violence toward people or animals.
Educational or documentary uses can be legitimate reasons to post violent content.
GitHub may restrict such content's visibility to people who opt in.
Next of kin, a designated successor, or another authorized person can request action on a deceased user's account.
A request must explain the requester's relationship to the deceased user.
The requester must say what action is sought, such as transferring public repositories or canceling billing.
GitHub may request identification, a death certificate, or evidence of authority before processing.
Excessive automated bulk activity is prohibited.
Fake accounts and automated inauthentic interactions are prohibited.
Automated starring or following used for rank abuse is prohibited.
Using GitHub servers to relay unsolicited advertising is prohibited.
Researchers may use public non-personal information only if resulting publications are open access.
Archivists may use public information for archival purposes.
The information-use rules apply regardless of scraping, API collection, or another collection route.
Service information may not be used for spam, including unsolicited emails or selling personal information.
Targeted personal attacks are prohibited harassment.
Orchestrating disruptive activity that amounts to abuse is prohibited.
Disagreement or downvoting alone may not rise to harassment.
Posting another person's personal information is prohibited.
Nonconsensual photos or videos may be an invasion of privacy, especially when they pose a safety risk.
GitHub considers whether reported information is already publicly available elsewhere.
Public information shared with intent to harass may violate the bullying and harassment policy.
Misrepresenting identity or association in a misleading way is prohibited.
A deceptively similar username or organization name can be impersonation when it misleads others.
A similar username alone is not necessarily impersonation; GitHub considers context.
Parody and satire consistent with acceptable-use rules are generally allowed.
False or deceptive content is prohibited under this policy when likely to harm the public or interfere with civic participation.
GitHub generally allows parody and satire consistent with its acceptable-use rules.
GitHub considers context such as disclaimers and credible citations when reviewing the content.
Projects designed to facilitate synthetic child sexual abuse material are prohibited.
Projects designed to facilitate violent extremist propaganda are prohibited.
Projects designed to facilitate nonconsensual sexually explicit media are prohibited.
GitHub examines project context, including configuration, marketing, and documentation, when assessing violations.
GitHub uses cookies to provide its websites.
GitHub uses cookies to secure its websites.
GitHub uses cookies to analyze website usage.
The published cookie list may change as cookie names and numbers change.
Candidate personal data is normally used only for the purpose for which it was collected.
A different compatible use requires a reasonable need and legal basis for further processing.
Data from exploring job openings may be processed for recruiting.
After successful application, candidate data may be processed to enter an employment relationship.
GitHub discloses candidate data only to recipients with a legitimate business need.
Disclosed data must be used consistently with the candidate privacy statement.
GitHub may disclose candidate data to third parties providing services for it.
GitHub may disclose candidate data to comply with legal obligations or lawful process.
Candidate-site cookies can store settings and enable sign-in.
Candidate-site cookies can combat fraud and measure service performance.
Web beacons help deliver cookies and collect usage or performance data.
Browser controls can limit cookies and clearing or blocking them can withdraw consent.
Service usage collection includes IP address, device and session details.
Website logs include the referring site, pages viewed, and links clicked.
Essential cookies support functions such as stored settings and recognition.
Non-essential analytics cookies may depend on jurisdiction and consent.
Participants agree to GitHub's Terms of Service.
Participants also agree to Acceptable Use Policies and the Community Code of Conduct.
GitHub investigates abuse reports and may moderate public Community content violating the terms or code.
The platform license is limited to compliant extension development and related interoperability purposes.
Violations may lead to extension removal, token revocation, or account or extension suspension.
Appeals may be submitted through GitHub's appeal and reinstatement process.
The partner must not resell GitHub products under the agreement.
The partner must not charge qualified users for use of GitHub products under the agreement.
The partner is responsible and liable for qualified users' use of the products.
The partner must cooperate with GitHub to enforce the agreement against misuse.
The partner must promptly end product access for users who no longer qualify.
Participants are expected to treat other participants with respect and courtesy.
Harassment of event participants is not tolerated.
Behavior reasonably making participants feel unsafe is not tolerated.
Event communication and behavior should suit a professional setting with varied backgrounds.
The Event Code of Conduct covers staff and sponsors as Event Participants.
An attendee must have capacity and authority to accept the Event Terms.
An attendee must agree to follow the Event Code of Conduct.
Where alcohol is served, the attendee must meet the stated age or local legal drinking age.
A participant asked to stop harassing or prohibited behavior must comply immediately.
Organizers may warn or expel a violator without a refund.
Pre-release software may fail or delete or corrupt data.
GitHub may change or discontinue a pre-release product without notice.
GitHub is not obligated to provide maintenance, support, or updates for the pre-release product.
GitHub assesses its business and supply chain for modern-slavery and child-labor risks.
GitHub prioritizes more severe, widespread, or probable risk areas for due diligence and monitoring.
GitHub obtains supplier assurances that their practices align with the statement and relevant law.
GitHub says it will audit existing suppliers and seek confirmation from higher-risk suppliers.
If GitHub directly caused such harm, it commits to remediation for victims.
Actions cannot be used for cryptomining.
Actions cannot be offered as a standalone or integrated commercial Actions service.
Disproportionate server burden, such as using Actions as a CDN or serverless app, is prohibited.
Misuse can cause job termination, use restrictions, repository disabling, or account suspension.
Maintainers can publish community-specific expectations for project interaction.
People with repository write access can edit, delete, or hide comments.
Authorized repository members can lock disruptive conversations.
An account or organization can block a user.
A public project can set temporary interaction limits when facing unwanted attention.
Extension developers must protect personal data and encrypt any stored personal data.
Extensions may not bypass access controls.
Extensions may not use unpublished APIs.
Extensions may not collect, store, or use personal data without proper user consent.
Contacting users outside GitHub requires a separate clear permission process, except for specified emergencies.
Individual users retain ultimate administrative control over their own accounts.
Individual users retain ultimate administrative control over content within their accounts.
The customer retains ultimate administrative control over organizations created for it.
The customer controls user-generated content in repositories within its organizations, subject to the corporate terms.
Urgent event problems should be reported directly to venue security or a GitHub employee.
Non-urgent issues can be emailed to GitHub's event contact.
Life-threatening situations call for dialing 911 immediately.
GitHub employees can help participants contact security or law enforcement or escort them to safety.
The developer is solely responsible for its Developer Products.
The developer grants GitHub a license to process and display the listing on Marketplace.
The developer must provide a separate EULA governing end-user rights to its products.
The EULA is between developer and end user.
GitHub is not responsible under the developer's EULA.
A US Marketplace user must be at least 13 years old.
A Marketplace user outside the US must meet that country's minimum age law.
A Marketplace user must have a valid GitHub account.
A Marketplace user must accept applicable GitHub Terms and Marketplace Terms.
A person accepting terms for an entity must have authority to bind that entity and its users.
The Software's open-source license and applicable component licenses appear in Open Source Notices.
Application Terms remain part of the agreement unless GitHub agrees otherwise in writing.
An open-source license governs a component only to the limited extent it expressly supersedes Application Terms.
The pre-release license permits non-production evaluation and testing.
Internal network deployment for evaluation is allowed.
Active production use, including live customer-data processing, is not allowed.
Non-public program information is confidential even without a confidentiality marking.
The participant may use confidential information only to provide program feedback.
The participant must not disclose program confidential information to third parties.
Legally compelled disclosure requires prior notice to GitHub.
Legally compelled disclosure requires efforts to limit disclosure and obtain confidential treatment.
The partner grants GitHub a perpetual and irrevocable license for token patterns used in security scanning or credential protection.
GitHub may sublicense token patterns only to affiliates and bound service providers.
GitHub may distribute software containing token patterns under MIT or another OSI-approved license.
Once open-source distributed, incorporated token patterns are not subject to recall or revocation.
The token-pattern license survives termination or expiration.
GitHub notifies affected users of the specific allegedly illegal content and the legal takedown request.
GitHub allows affected users to appeal the decision.
GitHub limits the takedown's geographic scope when possible.
GitHub posts the official request in its public government-takedowns repository.
Enterprise Server can be used to store ITAR or other export-controlled information.
End users remain responsible for ITAR and other export-control compliance.
Enterprise Server can usually be exported without a license to most destinations.
It may not be sold or exported to the specified Country Group E:1 destinations or named restricted Ukrainian regions.
Public user profiles display a username.
Public user profiles display starred repositories.
Users may optionally publish their real name.
GitHub may maintain private email addresses as private account data.
GitHub may maintain payment details as private account data.
GitHub may maintain security access logs as private account data.
GitHub generally notifies users about pending account or repository requests.
Notice may be omitted when law or a court order prohibits it.
Before disclosure, GitHub makes a reasonable effort to email affected owners a copy of the legal process so they can challenge it.
In rare urgent circumstances, GitHub may delay notice to prevent death or serious harm or because of an ongoing investigation.
Non-public user data is disclosed with user consent or valid legal process, subject to limited urgent circumstances.
A valid subpoena can obtain some non-public account information in an official civil or criminal investigation.
Account access logs require a qualifying court order or search warrant.
GitHub SIRT handles internal incident response when its constituency is affected.
GitHub SIRT does not provide incident response services to customers.
GitHub aims to give affected customers timely, accurate incident information for their own investigation.
SIRT triage investigates whether an incident occurred and its impact.
Even a small benefit can be improper when intended to influence someone.
Tickets to major events are examples of unacceptable customer gifts.
Low-cost bleacher-type sports tickets are examples of acceptable customer hospitality.
A reasonably priced dinner is an example of acceptable customer hospitality.
The commitment applies before GitHub brings a non-defensive claim arising from termination of a Covered License.
Stopping a violation provisionally reinstates the license unless the copyright holder finally terminates it.
Stopping a violation permanently reinstates the license if the copyright holder does not notify the violator within 60 days.
A first-time notice followed by cure within 30 days also permanently reinstates the license.
